title: The Biggest Group After Every New Friendship

concept.title: Union-find keeps the size of every group, so the largest size can be kept up to date
body: Friendships are added one by one. After each new friendship, how many people are in the **biggest group** of friends (a group is a set of people linked through chains of friends)? Recomputing the groups after every edge would take O(m * (n + m)). Union-find handles an edge in almost constant time, because it can **merge two groups and know the size of the result**.

Store the size of every group at its root. When an edge joins two different groups, the new group has the size `size[a] + size[b]`: update the running maximum with it. If the edge joins two people who are already in the same group, nothing changes. Printing the running maximum after every edge gives the answer.

body.code:
best = 1
for u, v in edges:
    a, b = find(u), find(v)
    if a != b:
        # attach the smaller group to the larger one
        if size[a] < size[b]:
            a, b = b, a
        parent[b] = a
        size[a] += size[b]
        best = max(best, size[a])
    print(best)

body: This is an *online* algorithm: it answers after each edge without looking at the future. The union-find operations (find with path compression, union by size) cost almost O(1), so the whole run is O((n + m) alpha(n)).

statement: There are `n` people and no friendships at first. Then `m` friendships are added one after another. After each one, print the size of the biggest group of people connected through chains of friends (at the beginning every group has one person, so the answer is at least 1). Print the `m` answers on one line.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge between the nodes `u` and `v`.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: After 1-2: {1, 2} has 2 people; after 3-4: still 2; after 2-3: {1, 2, 3, 4} has 4; after 4-5: all 5: 2 2 4 5.

hints: Keep the size of every group at its root.
When an edge joins two different groups, add the sizes and update the running maximum.
Print the maximum after every edge, even if the edge changed nothing.

explanation: Union-find stores the size of each group at its root; every real merge produces a group of the combined size, which updates the running maximum printed after each edge.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + m) alpha(n)), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

parent = []
size = []

def find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
        x = parent[x]
    return x

def union(a, b):
    a, b = find(a), find(b)
    if a == b:
        return False
    if size[a] < size[b]:
        a, b = b, a
    parent[b] = a
    size[a] += size[b]
    return True

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

parent.extend(range(n + 1))
size.extend([1] * (n + 1))
best = 1
out = []
for u, v in edges:
    if union(u, v):
        best = max(best, size[find(u)])
    out.append(best)
print(*out)
